public_rationale: Continued sales are supported. The loss-making and causal components remain unestablished. Microsoft's later report of demand exceeding supply challenges the surplus-capacity story, but does not measure the exact baseline in the claim. No decisive event meets the early-resolution rule, and the financial assertion has no specified accounting basis.
limitations: Evidence supports only one component of the compound forecast.
Company statements about demand are not independent utilization measurements.
An unknown accounting basis prevents a supported or contradicted financial verdict.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Microsoft will continue selling unprofitable generative AI software because its current capacity exceeds the limited demand.

statement.excerpt: I actually believe it will continue selling this unprofitable, unsustainable software, because the capacity it has right now is more than sufficient to deal with the lack of demand.

from_speaker: the capacity it has right now
our_interpretation: The forecast combines continued sales, losses attributable to Microsoft's generative AI software, and a causal explanation based on surplus capacity.
Current capacity means capacity available when the post appeared on March 3, 2025.
No deadline or duration is supplied. I do not add one.
Profitability requires attributable revenue and costs. Microsoft's consolidated earnings or its investment gains and losses cannot establish software profitability.
The words supply no accounting basis for the profitability assertion.
criteria.support_condition: Microsoft continues selling generative AI software at an attributable loss, and dated evidence establishes that surplus March 2025 capacity relative to demand explains that decision.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Direct evidence disproves a necessary component, such as attributable profitability over the relevant continuation period or an actual capacity shortage at the stated March 2025 baseline.
